study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Italinna et al., PLOS Computational Biology, 2023
study_identification_part.si4_title: Using normative modeling and machine learning for detecting mild traumatic brain injury from magnetoencephalography data

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Detect mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) from resting-state MEG by computing deviation (z-score) maps relative to a large normative dataset and classifying patients vs controls using SVM.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: The normative reference data are explicitly stated as Cam-CAN.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: A large open neuroimaging dataset by the Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience (Cam-CAN) ... was used for creating the normative reference data.

rci2_hc_n.reason: Subjects with missing or incomplete data were excluded, resulting in 621 subjects in the normative set.
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: Subjects with missing or incomplete resting-state MEG measurements or T1-weighted MRI images were excluded from the analyses, resulting in a set of 621 subjects.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Using normative deviation maps from MEG, an SVM classified mTBI vs controls with ~79% accuracy; theta-band deviations were most informative.
